tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (slow endpoints, throttling, silent failures, scale-to-zero questions) rather than internal mechanics, explicitly covers many trigger contexts including cases where the user doesn't name the domain directly ('even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency...'), and while lengthy, stays within a dense paragraph form appropriate for the complexity of the domain.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a serverless endpoint is slow or throttled after idle periods... even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency, SNS topics, InputLocation, backlog scaling or AsyncInferenceConfig by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body avoids explaining general concepts and jumps directly into domain-specific check catalogs, API quirks, and routing tables specific to SageMaker serverless/async inference.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: Detailed reference data (full check definitions, metric semantics, API detail) is kept in references/ files; the body only has a short index table and router pointing to them, not the full detail.
tests.evidence: The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file in references/ is linked via markdown link syntax in the body (checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md, collection-reference.md, metrics-and-logs.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, api-quirks.md, known-causes.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is paired with a specific trigger condition for loading (e.g., matching symptom, before assigning check-id, when metric is empty).
tests.evidence: Load it before assigning any check-id or severity... load it before interpreting any empty metric or InService state

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ without traversal or absolute paths.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, check-id assignment, read-only API usage) are prescriptive with explicit do/don't rules, while flexible areas (break-fix diagnosis, review procedure) explain rationale and allow judgment.
tests.evidence: Never call CreateEndpoint (including serverless/async), a scaling mutation... Recommend the fix and give the exact CLI/IaC command; let the user run it.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools as equal options; it routes to a single prescribed API/metric per symptom in the Router table.
tests.evidence: | The first request after idle is very slow, cold start is bad | `DescribeEndpointConfig` `ServerlessConfig`, then `ModelSetupTime` in CloudWatch |

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (match symptom → load check catalog → confirm via collection calls → report with check-id) applicable to any serverless/async endpoint, not a one-off instance.
tests.evidence: Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has explicit 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' sections documenting non-obvious pitfalls like misleading CloudWatch datapoints and InService states.
tests.evidence: "No `ModelSetupTime` datapoints came back, so there is no cold start and the backlog is empty." Absent CloudWatch datapoints mean no traffic or nothing emitted in the window, not a measured zero.
